name: How to Spot Bad SNT: A Street-Level Survival Guide
author: Anonymous, distributed via dead-drop in Hamtramck Enclave
body:
If you're going to a ripper, you need to know what good SNT looks like. Your life depends on it.

GENUINE GEN 7 SNT: — Color: pale amber, translucent, with visible capillary network (looks like very thin honey with red threads) — Texture: slightly sticky, elastic, does not tear easily — Smell: faint metallic-sweet (like copper and vanilla) — Temperature: room temperature or slightly above (living tissue generates minimal heat) — Packaging: vacuum-sealed in opaque medical-grade polymer with holographic Cortex Dynamics or Tessera BioSystems authentication seal — Expiration: SNT has a 6-month Gray Zone life from manufacture. Check the date. If there's no date, walk away.

RED FLAGS: — Pure white or grey color (dead or synthetic substitute) — No visible capillary network (may be inert scaffold) — Brittle or crumbly texture (degraded or expired) — Strong chemical smell (industrial sealant disguised as SNT) — Packaging with misspellings, low-resolution logos, or no authentication seal — Temperature significantly above room temp (bacterial contamination) — Price below Φ150/cm² (nobody sells genuine SNT at a loss)

IF YOUR RIPPER WON'T LET YOU INSPECT THE SNT: Leave. Immediately. A good ripper shows you the product. They show you the authentication seal. They let you hold it. They answer your questions. If they refuse, they're hiding something, and the thing they're hiding will be inside your body.

IF YOU'VE ALREADY BEEN INSTALLED WITH SUSPECT SNT: Watch for: persistent warmth at the implant site after week 3 (should normalize by then), loss of sensation in the implant (should be increasing, not decreasing), visible darkening of skin around the bonding margin, or any fluid discharge. If you see any of these, get to a real hospital. Tell them what happened. They won't judge. They've seen it before. They see it every day.
